It is further submitted by Mr. Bhoi, learned counsel that the Petitioner is entitled to compensation as per the market value of the land on the date of acquisition.
He is also entitled to rehabilitation and resettlement benefit.
Thus, he prays for a direction to Opposite Party No.2 to award adequate compensation and extend rehabilitation and resettlement benefit in favour of the Petitioner.
5. Mr. Behura, learned Additional Government Advocate submits that the writ petition is not maintainable, as the Petitioner has not exhausted the remedy under Section 64 of the Act.

It is his submission that since the Act itself provides adequate remedy for enhancement of compensation,
which has not yet been availed by the Petitioner.
As such, the writ petition is not maintainable.

6. Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court finds that the Zone Officer-cum-Land Acquisition Collector, Subarnrekha Irrigation Project, Bahalda Zone,
Baripada, Mayurbhanj-Opposite Party No.2 assessed the compensation and communicated it to the Petitioner vide Letter dated 2nd June, 2023 (Annexure-3).
Being aggrieved, the Petitioner submitted a grievance petition before him on 21st June, 2024.
On perusal of Annexure-4 (copy of the Petitioner's written grievance), it appears that the same is not in terms of Section 64 of the Act.

6.1 It is, therefore, submitted by Mr. Bhoi, learned counsel for the Petitioner that a properly constituted petition under Section 64 Designation: JUNIOR STENOGRAPHER Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack Date: 07-Jan-2026 13:55:10 of the Act shall be filed before Opposite Party No.2 for his consideration.
7. It appears that the award was communicated to the Petitioner on 2nd June, 2023 and in the meantime two years has already been elapsed.
Thus, the Collector, Mayurbhanj will not be in a position to entertain an application under Section 64 of the Act beyond one year, as provided under 2nd proviso to Section 64 (2) of the Act.

8. Taking into consideration that the Petitioner has filed an application redressing his grievances before Opposite Party No.2 on 21st June, 2024 with an impression that his grievances will be redressed for enhancement of compensation, it is directed that in the event the Petitioner files an application under Section 64 of the Act before the Collector, Mayurbhanj within a period of three weeks hence along with relevant documents and information, the same shall be considered on its own merit for reference to the Authority without adhering to the technicalities under the 2nd proviso to Section 64(2) of the Act within a period of one month thereafter and the decision thereof shall be communicated to the Petitioner forthwith.
Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
